newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares higher ahead of rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares higher ahead of rate decision.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Monday after two days of losses, as investors waited for the Bank of Israel interest rate announcement, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 2.02 percent, or 4.68 points, to 236.59 on all-share turnover of 132 million shekels against 126 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 2.13 percent higher at 245.51.
After the close of trading the Bank of Israel said it was lowering its key lending rate for February by 0.5 percentage point to an annualised 14.2 percent.

"The market is recovering from Sunday's fall (in which the market plunged 3.6 percent). The main reason for today's rise was that investors expect a rate cut of 0.5 percentage point and hope that the central bank will raise the reserve requirement," said Ari Eidelheit at Zeller Eblagon Securities.
Financial sources said a few weeks ago that the Bank of Israel might raise the reserve requirement for commercial banks in an effort to combat growing liquidity in the economy.

"It was (the level) expected, no surprises. They put a lot of pressure on (Bank of Israel Governor Jacob) Frenkel to lower more but he was very cautious. It won't influence shares or the forex market," said Tzvi Hoffman of Meitav Securities and Investments.

"I believe that the market has reached a ceiling and that it will stabilise at the current level. From now on trading will be very selective as investors wait for the release of fourth-quarter earning reports," Eidelheit added.

The most active shares were Bank Haopalim, which rose 2.75 percent to 589 agorot on volume of 8.0 million shekels; Koor Industries, which gained 2.5 percent to 32,108 agorot on turnover of 7.0 million shekels; and Israel Chemicals, which rose 2.75 percent to 350 agorot on turnover of 6.9 million shekels.
